model.html:
Level: INE median €/m² of T3 flats actually sold in the parish (2026Q2: €4,429/m², a 12-month rolling median, so it lags ~6 months). Month-to-month movement: INE's bank-appraisal median for Lisbon apartments (to 2026-09). Typical 122 m² T3 today ≈ €570,037.

Purchase €555,000 vs typical €404,899 then (+37%): part renovation + lift + micro-location, part the 2021 Golden-Visa buying rush (Lisbon's residential route closed Jan 2022). That premium fades with a 4-yr half-life toward the live peer premium: 6 distinct renovated lift-served listings of 33 seen in the last 90 days (re-posts of the same flat counted once), at asking −7% → +10% vs typical. Premium now +20%.

Honesty check on the index: INE's parish figure is centred on Dec 2025, 11 months back; the gap is bridged with the appraisal index. Replayed on INE's own history (16 past quarters), that bridge missed the parish level INE later published by ±11% (RMSE) – no better than holding the level flat (±10%), though less biased while prices rise. So it is used for direction, and that error is in the range.

80% range, in log points: peer-to-peer spread 0.17 (the part the purchase price no longer pins), peer-median error 0.09, asking-to-sale gap ±0.03, index 0.11 → total ±18% (1 sd).

*“As this flat” = asking × (122 m² / its m²)^0.9 × (1 − 7% asking-to-sale gap).
